s: A company wants to migrate its on-premises application to AWS. The database for the application stores structured product data and temporary user session data. The company needs to decouple the product data from the user session data. The company also needs to implement replication in another AWS Region for disaster recovery. Which solution will meet these requirements with the HIGHEST performance?
o: Create an Amazon RDS DB instance with separate schemas to host the product data and the user session data. Configure a read replica for the DB instance in another Region.

Create an Amazon RDS DB instance to host the product data. Configure a read replica for the DB instance in another Region. Create a global datastore in Amazon ElastiCache for Memcached to host the user session data.
Create two Amazon DynamoDB global tables. Use one global table to host the product data Use the other global table to host the user session data. Use DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) for caching.
Create an Amazon RDS DB instance to host the product data. Configure a read replica for the DB instance in another Region. Create an Amazon DynamoDB global table to host the user session data
x: ElastiCache Global Datastore works only with Redis/Valkey, not Memcached, so B can't replicate sessions to another Region. RDS with a cross-Region read replica for products and a DynamoDB global table for sessions gives fast, replicated storage for both.

w.y: Product data and session data must live in separate stores, and each store needs cross-Region replication. RDS with a cross-Region read replica covers the structured product data. A DynamoDB global table gives single-digit-millisecond, multi-Region replicated storage for session data. This is the only option where both stores actually replicate to another Region.

o.A: Separate schemas in one instance don't decouple the workloads: session churn still competes with product queries on the same database.
o.B: ElastiCache Global Datastore supports only Redis OSS and Valkey, not Memcached, so the sessions can't be replicated to another Region.
o.C: Workable, but DAX is a Regional in-memory cache that is not replicated, and moving relational product data to DynamoDB requires redesigning the data model.
o.D: Correct: RDS with a cross-Region read replica for products and a DynamoDB global table for sessions gives fast, replicated storage for both.

s: Replication across AWS Regions using global datastores - Amazon ElastiCache
Global tables - multi-active, multi-Region replication - Amazon DynamoDB
